author: chrysostom
title: Homilies on the Epistle of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans
edition: The Oxford Translation (Library of the Fathers), revised by W. H. Simcox; edited by Philip Schaff with notes by George B. Stevens; Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Series 1, Vol. 11 (1889)
translation: Translated by J. B. Morris for the Library of the Fathers, revised by W. H. Simcox; Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Series 1, Vol. 11 (1889)

rights.worldwide: to confirm: death dates of every author, translator and editor named (life + 70 years); J. B. Morris died in 1880, W. H. Simcox in 1889, George B. Stevens in 1906, Philip Schaff in 1893

notes: The thirty-two homilies are CCEL npnf111 sections vii.iii–vii.xxxiv; the Argument before them (vii.ii) is not included. This translation prints no section numbers, so a locus names the homily only. Each verse mark the homily prints ('Ver. 9.', 'Chap. ii. ver. 1.') opens an entry; what comes before the first mark is on the verses of the homily's heading. Every paragraph of a homily's exposition is kept, in the order printed, in entries of up to about 350 words; a paragraph cut between entries is marked with ' ...'. Each homily's closing exhortation is left out, from the first sentence after the last verse mark that exhorts the hearers ('Let us then...'); the whole homilies are in library/texts/. Homily XXVII is headed 'Rom. XIV. 25-27': Chrysostom's text has the closing doxology after 14:23, as many Greek manuscripts do, so its entries are on Romans 16:25-27. Homily VI prints 'Ver. 12.' over Romans 2:28 ('For he is not a Jew which is one outwardly'), between ver. 27 and 29; that entry is on 2:28. The translator's footnotes and the notes on manuscript readings are left out.
